definition: Rattle GUI is a free and open source software (GNU GPL v2) package providing a graphical user interface (GUI) for data mining using the R statistical programming language.
details: Rattle is used in a variety of situations. Currently there are 15 different government departments in Australia, in addition to various other organisations around the world, which use Rattle in their data mining activities and as a statistical package. Rattle provides considerable data mining functionality by exposing the power of the R Statistical Software through a graphical user interface. Rattle is also used as a teaching facility to learn the R software Language. There is a Log Code tab, which replicates the R code for any activity undertaken in the GUI, which can be copied and pasted. Rattle can be used for statistical analysis, or model generation. Rattle allows for the dataset to be partitioned into training, validation and testing. The dataset can be viewed and edited. There is also an option for scoring an external data file. Rattle was originally released in early 2006 and relaunched in 2025. The relaunch replaced the dated R interface with a modern look using the Flutter framework and includes new modules to input R code as well predefined code modules.

explainer.lead: Rattle GUI is a free and open source (GNU GPL v2) graphical interface for data mining using the R statistical programming language. It matters because it exposes R's data mining power without requiring users to write R code directly.

tiers.eli5: It is a point-and-click front end that lets you do data analysis in R without typing commands.
tiers.practitioner: Analysts use it for data mining tasks and as a teaching facility for learning R; a pitfall is that it is not an automation tool—its Log Code tab shows the underlying R code for reuse.
tiers.paperLevel: A GNU GPL v2 package providing a graphical user interface for data mining with the R statistical language; it exposes R's functionality through a GUI and is used by 15 Australian government departments plus other organisations worldwide, and as a teaching facility with a Log Code tab showing generated R code.

explainer.example: Load a dataset in Rattle, run a model through the GUI, then copy the generated R code from the Log Code tab.
